variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: photorealistic residential cabinet-design comparison, one clean single-camera landscape image.
Input Image 1 is the edit target and sole geometry/camera anchor: a verified Blender rendering of this homeowner's actual corridor cabinet, candidate version. Reconstruct its surfaces as a convincing photograph while preserving this exact cabinet composition, footprint, proportions and crop.
Homeowner requirements: a modern Japanese minimal warm interior, but this cabinet may have its own color and style rather than matching every cabinet in the home. The entire 4500 mm long, 400 mm deep cabinet must meet the flat ceiling directly at 2750 mm: use the existing slim matching top scribe panel touching the ceiling, ZERO open space over the cabinet. Do not introduce an open dark gap, cove, crown molding or ceiling light trough.
Geometry locks: preserve the exact cabinet panel layout in the reference. Preserve the SINGLE VERY SHALLOW rectangular wood niche near the entrance at IMAGE LEFT, only 200 mm clear height, bottom 1200 mm and top 1400 mm above floor, about 960 mm clear width. It is a slim slot for keys, not a tall display alcove or full-length recess. Keep its original single dark shallow tray and small warm light. Preserve the low white TV console visible at image right, the window/opening at image left, pale oak floor, warm plain ceiling, wall positions, and existing cropped dining-chair fragments at bottom. No extra objects or display shelves.
Materials and light: physically believable matte cabinetry, fine subtle wood grain, soft daylight with restrained warm interior light. Warm white stays distinguishable from yellow. Keep dark colors readable. Real photographic detail and natural highlights; no staged extra accessories.
Camera: same near-frontal view, height and framing as the reference, single image only, no collage, no split screen. Keep the cabinet top-to-ceiling junction clearly visible and all cabinet ends in frame. No text, labels, logos, UI or watermarks.

Designer solution A — soft warm sand-grey and pale oak: matching warm greige/sand matte flat cabinet fronts (concept sRGB #B8AA96), slightly stony warm-neutral rather than pure white or orange-beige. Hide opening hardware as in the reference. Pale natural oak only in the shallow left niche. Keep the cabinet flat and calm, with subtle precise panel joints. All adjacent cabinets retain their original finishes. Do not add a wooden end bay in this option.
Distinctive marker: Cabinet option A sand oak full ceiling.

Designer solution B — muted olive-sage and a pale oak end bay: the main fronts are low-saturation grey olive green (concept sRGB #7C8974). Preserve the ONE approximately 650 mm wide PALE OAK vertical end bay at IMAGE RIGHT next to the TV console, including its rounded outer end of about R80 mm. This is a CLOSED wood cabinet bay, not an open shelf. Preserve the subtle slim inset oak pulls and pale oak-lined shallow left niche. Keep the matching slim green top scribe touching the ceiling, as in the reference. The green is soft sage/olive, not vivid grass green, mint or dark forest green. Do not turn the whole cabinet into wood.
